GE Predix Alternatives 2026: Asset Integrity Migration

GE split into three companies in 2024. Here's what happened to Predix/APM and how to evaluate migration options in 2026.

By Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III · July 24, 2026

GE Predix alternatives are asset integrity and industrial IoT platforms that operators evaluate as replacements for GE's legacy Predix stack, whose asset performance management (APM) capability now sits inside GE Vernova following GE's April 2024 three-way corporate split. Operators migrate for reasons ranging from platform consolidation and licensing changes to the need for tighter native integration between 3D visualization and inspection data than the legacy Predix architecture offered.

If your team is running an evaluation in 2026, it helps to understand exactly where the product landed after the breakup, why other operators are moving, and what to check for in a replacement before you sign anything.

What Is GE Predix and Why Are Companies Migrating Away From It?

Predix was GE Digital's industrial IoT platform, launched in the mid-2010s as GE's bet on an "operating system for industry." Over time, GE narrowed its focus from a broad PaaS play to a more targeted Asset Performance Management (APM) product line, and much of the original Predix branding was retired well before 2026. Operators cite a few consistent migration drivers: platform direction has shifted multiple times as GE reorganized its software business, integration between APM, digital twin visualization, and inspection workflows historically required significant custom engineering, and total cost of ownership for large legacy contracts has become harder to justify against newer, purpose-built asset integrity platforms.

The 2024 GE Breakup: Where Predix and APM Live Now

In April 2024, General Electric completed its planned separation into three independent, publicly traded companies: GE Aerospace (retaining the GE name and jet engine business), GE HealthCare (spun off in January 2023), and GE Vernova (energy — power generation, wind, electrification, and grid software). GE Digital's industrial software portfolio, including Asset Performance Management (APM) and the remaining Predix-derived capabilities, was carried into GE Vernova as part of its Electrification Software segment. This matters practically: your GE APM contract, support relationship, and roadmap now run through GE Vernova, not the aerospace-focused GE entity, and the product's investment priorities are shaped by GE Vernova's energy-transition strategy rather than a horizontal industrial IoT vision.

Why Operators Are Evaluating Alternatives in 2026

Three factors are driving renewed evaluation activity in 2026. First, contract renewal cycles from the original Predix-era deals (many signed 2016-2019) are hitting their second or third renewal, prompting procurement to re-benchmark the market rather than auto-renew. Second, GE Vernova's software roadmap is understandably weighted toward power generation and grid customers, which can leave downstream oil & gas, refining, and marine asset integrity use cases feeling like a secondary priority. Third, the broader digital twin market has matured — platforms purpose-built around NDT inspection data, RBI, and API 579 fitness-for-service now exist that didn't in Predix's original design era, and they integrate visualization and integrity calculations natively rather than through custom middleware.

Key Evaluation Criteria for a Replacement

When benchmarking alternatives, evaluate against a consistent scorecard rather than a feature checklist supplied by any single vendor:

  • Native NDT and RBI integration — can the platform ingest UT/RT/MT/PT/TOFD/phased array data natively and map it to CMLs, or does it require a third-party integration layer?
  • Fitness-for-service capability — does it run API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 assessments directly, or export data for offline engineering calculations?
  • EAM/historian integration — proven connectors to SAP PM, IBM Maximo, and OSIsoft/AVEVA PI without heavy custom development.
  • Data migration path — can historical inspection and corrosion data be imported without manual re-entry?
  • Deployment flexibility — cloud, on-premise, or hybrid options for operators with data residency or OT network security constraints.
  • Total cost of ownership — licensing, implementation, and ongoing support cost relative to the scope of asset classes covered.

Top Alternatives Compared

The current landscape includes a mix of legacy enterprise APM vendors and newer, purpose-built digital twin platforms. Siemens Mindsphere (now part of Siemens Xcelerator) offers strong OT integration for Siemens-heavy plants but carries similar platform-lock-in tradeoffs to Predix. Cognite Data Fusion has built a strong reputation for industrial data contextualization but is priced and positioned toward large enterprise data engineering teams rather than inspection-first workflows. Purpose-built asset integrity digital twin platforms like Atlantis's digital twin platform take a different approach — 3D visualization with native NDT, RBI, and API 579 FFS built in from day one rather than layered on top of a general IoT platform. Migration Roadmap: Moving Off Predix Without Losing Historical Data

The single biggest risk in any Predix migration is losing years of accumulated inspection and corrosion-rate history. A sound migration plan starts with a full export of asset hierarchy, CML/TML data, thickness readings, and RBI risk scores from the legacy system, followed by a validation pass comparing corrosion rate trends and remaining-life calculations in the new platform against the old ones for a sample of critical assets before cutover. Run both systems in parallel for at least one inspection cycle on high-consequence equipment to confirm the new platform's FFS outputs match engineering expectations. Only after that validation should you decommission the legacy system.

Data Migration Checklist

  • Full asset hierarchy and equipment tag export with CML/TML coordinates
  • Complete UT, RT, MT, PT, TOFD, and phased array inspection history, not just latest readings
  • RBI risk scores and damage mechanism assignments per API 580/581
  • Historian tag mapping for operating temperature/pressure context (OSIsoft/AVEVA PI)
  • EAM work order history linked to affected CMLs (SAP PM / IBM Maximo)
  • Parallel-run validation on at least 10-15% of critical assets before full cutover

Estimating the financial case for migration is worth doing formally rather than on gut feel — the digital twin ROI calculator models inspection efficiency and deferred-failure savings against implementation cost. Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: Is GE Predix still available in 2026?

A: The original standalone Predix platform was retired in earlier years as GE narrowed focus to Asset Performance Management (APM). Following GE's April 2024 corporate split, APM and related industrial software now operate under GE Vernova's Electrification Software segment.

Q2: Which GE entity owns asset integrity software after the 2024 split?

A: GE Vernova, the energy-focused company created in the split, owns GE's industrial software portfolio including Asset Performance Management. GE Aerospace and GE HealthCare are separate, unrelated entities focused on aviation and medical technology respectively.

Q3: How long does migrating off Predix/GE Vernova APM typically take?

A: A well-scoped migration with historical data validation typically runs 3-6 months for a single asset class, with full parallel-run verification on critical equipment, and longer for enterprise-wide portfolios spanning multiple sites and asset types.

Q4: Will I lose historical inspection data when migrating?

A: Not if the migration plan includes a full export and validated import of CML/TML history, thickness readings, and RBI scores. Data loss typically only occurs when teams attempt a rushed cutover without a parallel validation period.

Q5: What should I prioritize when evaluating a Predix replacement?

A: Prioritize native NDT and RBI data integration, built-in API 579 fitness-for-service calculations, proven EAM/historian connectors, and a clear data migration path — these determine whether the new platform actually reduces engineering workload or just relocates the same manual effort.
